items.title: Larry Gold interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 18, 2025
items.q: I worked on records that he played on, but I don't think I ever worked with him, no.

ctx.x: You'll be — I think it's 504 or so.

There you go. So you know they have something they can go look, if they find a name that all of a sudden if they find Bernard Purdie, oh, what's up, he invented a shuffle? Oh let me go put his name in. And then they can get a hit off of that. You know what I mean? It's like that's important stuff. It's like that makes this as respectful as classical music was. You know? Where I read something recently about the history of the cello. You know that was written like 75 years ago. You know? And it was fascinating to…

Here's a little — why this just occurred to me — the baritone saxophone and the cello, especially a baritone saxophone with a low A and the cello are like this. They have the same range and I had a student here who played one of the Bach unaccompanied cello suites on the baritone saxophone. It was awesome except there's no place to breathe.
